name: Water-shifting storm shelter
subtitle: a spacecraft's water moved to block solar storms

effects.effect: a voltage across a wet porous material makes the liquid flow

effect: a voltage across a wet porous material makes the liquid flow
how: Crews bound for Mars face solar storms that can deliver a dangerous dose in hours, and shielding the whole ship is too heavy to launch. The ship's water is kept in porous wall panels, and when a storm is spotted a voltage drives it through the pores (electro-osmosis) into the wall facing the Sun, building a thick shield on just that side with no pumps to fail.
obstacle: Electro-osmosis is slow, so moving tonnes of water in the hour or so of warning needs very large panels.
why: Mass is what limits deep-space shielding; reusing water as a movable wall saves launches.
real: Reconfigurable water storm shelters (NASA RadWorks water wall, TransHab fill/drain tank) and repositionable shield patents exist, but none moves water by electro-osmosis through porous walls.
